title: Signal, Temporary for Type CD954 Standard (Without Luminaire Arm)
summary: Shows a temporary traffic signal on a Type CD954 standard without a luminaire arm, set on a 60" x 60" x 3/4" steel plate weighted with precast concrete blocks and tied with coil chain. The mast arm is limited to 15'-0" and carries one 3-section head at its end, with up to two 5-section heads and two pedestrian heads on the shaft. Temporary overhead signal wires may span a maximum of 100 feet.

sheets.notes:
Notes:
1. The CD954 standard (without luminaire arm) shall conform to Dept. of Transportation, City of Los Angeles Standard Dwg. # S-51.9.6 (foundation excluded).
2. The mast arm length shall not exceed 15'-0".
3. There shall be a maximum of 2 - 5 section signal heads and 2 - ped. heads mounted to the shaft and one 3-section signal head mounted at the end of mast arm.

Plan
60" x 60" x 3/4" steel plate. Tie with 3/8" coil chain. 25" x 3" x 1/2" angles welded to plate. 23" x 23" x 30" precast conc. block (4 req.). 23" x 13" x 30" precast conc. block (4 req.). Drill holes (4 req.) to accommodate 1-1/8" bolt size and 11-1/2" bolt circle. 3/8" cable, embed 12" deep (8 req.).

Section A-A
1-1/8" x 4" hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.). Weld bolts to 3/4" plate. 4" x 4" x 1/4" plate washer (4 req.). Level by mortar leveling bed, wedge edges until mortar sets (mortar is not required on C.A.B., dirt or when slope is less than 1/4" per ft.). A.C. or P.C.C. surface. Coat plate assembly with primer and traffic signal yellow paint.

Elevation
Type CD954 std. (without luminaire arm). Temporary O.H. signal wires (maximum span 100 feet). Mast arm 15'-0" max. All 12" sections. 2 signal heads, 2 pedestrian heads, street name sign. See plan and Section A-A.

The 60" x 60" x 3/4" steel plate is tied with 3/8" coil chain to precast concrete blocks and bolted with four 1-1/8" x 4" bolts. The mast arm is limited to 15'-0" and all signal heads must be polycarbonate.

sheets.notes:
Notes:
The CD954 standard shall conform to Dept. of Transportation, City of Los Angeles, Standard Drawing # S-51.9.6 (foundation excluded).
1. Temporary O.H. signal cable (maximum span 100 feet).
2. The mast arm length shall not exceed 15'-0".
3. There shall be a maximum of 2 - 5 section signal heads and 2 - ped. heads mounted to the shaft and one 3-section signal head mounted at the end of mast arm. All signal heads to be polycarbonate type.

Elevation
Type CD954 std. Mast arm 15'-0" max. All 12" sections. 6" min. Signal heads (see Note 3). 2 pedestrian heads. Street name sign. See plan and Section A-A. Roadway.

Plan
Tie with 3/8" coil chain. 60" steel plate. Weld angles to plate. 23" x 13" x 30" precast concrete block (4 req.). 2" hole. 4" x 4" x 1/2" plate washer (4 req.). Drill 1-1/2" diameter holes (4 req.) for 1-1/8" bolt size and 11-1/2" bolt circle. 3/8" cable, embed 12" deep (8 req.).

Section A-A
1-1/8" x 4" hex. hd. bolt, hex. nut, flat washer (4 req.). Weld bolts and 4" x 4" x 1/2" plate washers to 3/4" plate. 4" x 4" x 1/2" plate washer (4 req.). A.C. or P.C.C. surface. 60" x 60" x 3/4" steel plate. Level by mortar, wedge edges until mortar sets (mortar is not required on C.A.B., dirt or when slope is less than 1/4" per foot). Coat plate assembly with primer and traffic signal yellow paint.

Item "C" (Pelco AB-103).

title: Special Mast Arm Mountings (Sheet 2 of 2)
summary: Gives the notes explaining when to use mounting items A through E, which are Pelco products or equivalent. Item A is the basic mast arm mounting with a 6" tenon, B mounts standard heads, C mounts programmed visibility heads, D mounts electric signs, and E is the clamp kit. The standard 29" band fits 4" to 8.6" diameters and bands up to 56" can be used for larger poles. Detail A shows a 4-1/2" x 4-1/2" x 1/4" aluminum plate for sign box reinforcement.

sheets.notes:
Notes:
1. Item "A" is the basic mounting design for most mast arm signal installations when standard tenon location on the mast arm cannot be utilized. It uses a 6" tenon length with 2-3/8" outside diameter for plumbizer mounting.
2. Item "B" is used for installation of traffic signal heads, except programmed visibility (P.V.) heads, when it is desired to mount them horizontally or to adjust the height vertically by movement of item "E".
3. Item "C" is used for installation of horizontal or vertical programmed visibility (P.V.) heads. It is equipped with 14" arms which allow for replacement of signal lamps located in the rear of the signal head.
4. Item "D" is used for installation of electric signs.
5. Item "E" is a standard clamp kit designed to be used for fastening items "B", "C", and "D" to mast arms or poles in a vertical or horizontal position.
6. The bottom arms in items "B", "C", and "D" are stationary and are held in place with pipe threads and set screws. The upper arms slide along the shaft and are held in place with set screws.
7. The standard 29" band for items "A" and "E" fits a 4" to 8.6" diameter. Band lengths up to 56" can be used for larger diameter installations.
8. Items "A" through "E" are available from Pelco Products Inc. or equivalent.
9. The 1-1/2" x 1-1/2" aluminum lock nut shown with item "D" is commonly used for signal head and pedestrian head installations.
10. The 4-1/2" x 4-1/2" x 1/4" aluminum plate is used for sign box reinforcement at bracket installation location and must be specially fabricated.

Detail "A": 4-1/2" x 4-1/2" x 1/4" aluminum plate (not to scale)

title: Inductive Loop Installation
summary: Shows how to install inductive detector loops in a pavement sawcut, including winding details, slot sections, and the lead-in to a pullbox. Each detector gets 3 clockwise turns of loop wire unless the signal plan shows otherwise. The slot is filled with loop sealant to within 1/16" of the top, no more than 8 wires go in each sawcut slot, and loop wire is twisted at least 2 turns per foot. Slot depth must not exceed the pavement depth, and concrete (P.C.C.) surfaces need at least 2.5" of cover over the loop wire.

sheets.notes:
Winding details (not to scale)
Loop 1, loop 2. Direction of traffic flow. 3'-0" max. to pullbox. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair to pullbox.
Fill slot with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill).

Section A-A: 3" min.* (see Note 1). 1/2" max.
Section B-B and Section C-C: 5" min.* 8 wires maximum per sawcut slot. 1/2" max.

* Depth of slot not to exceed depth of pavement. For P.C.C. (concrete) surfaces, the minimum cover above loop wire shall be 2.5" minimum.

Notes:
1. Install 3 clockwise turns of loop wire for each detector, unless otherwise shown on signal plan.
2. See LADOT Material Specification No. 92-081-05 or latest revision.
3. Any non-round shaped loops must conform to all other specifications shown on this standard drawing.

title: Inductive Loop Installation (Sheet 2)
summary: Gives the sequence for installing inductive loops and the stub-out detail from the street to the pullbox. The pavement is opened at least 42" from the curb face and at least 18" from the edge of gutter, with an opening of no more than 12" x 16". A 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) conduit with a 45 degree elbow runs from the pullbox pit, at least 18" below street grade, and each stub-out carries no more than 8 loops or 16 wires.

sheets.notes:
Section D-D (not to scale)
Curb and gutter. 42" min. Hot patch asphalt concrete. 16" max. 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex. Existing pavement. Loop wires, 16" max. Loop sealant.

Stub-out detail (top view, not to scale)
Existing pavement, sand, sub base, hot patch asphalt concrete, 2" PVC or PVC conduit, 2" PVC flex conduit.

Notes: Perform loop installation in the following order:
1. Open the pavement at least 42" from curb face and at least 18" from edge of gutter using a star drill or a jack hammer (asphalt concrete only). Open no more than a 12" x 16" area. In cases where there is a concrete bus pad adjacent to the gutter, install the stub-out beyond the edge of the bus pad.
2. Install 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) from the pullbox pit with a 45 degree elbow at the stub-out as shown. Depth of the conduit shall be at least 18" below street grade.
3. Patch street using hot patch asphalt concrete and sand as shown.
4. Install duct seal where wires enter 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex.
5. Fill sawcut slot with Caltrans approved hot-melt rubberized asphalt sealant. No more than 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out.

title: Preformed Loop Installation
summary: Shows a preformed detector loop built from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene with a 3/4" O.D., with 4 turns of continuous #16 TFFN wire, and filled with hot rubberized asphalt. Each loop head has a 5" contraction/expansion joint with a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide, and the 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose runs in 2" PVC conduit from the pullbox to the pavement slab. Lead-in wires are twisted at least 2 times per foot, and any variation needs design engineer approval.

sheets.notes:
Winding details (not to scale)
6' expansion joint. CPVC tee. 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. CVPC cross. Expansion joint. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) to pullbox. 3'-0" max. Twisted tail.

Section A-A (not to scale)
Detector loop conductors. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Pavement. To detector per plan. Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see Note 7) (typical).

Notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, with an O.D. of 3/4" inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wires in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose with seamless fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a Schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.
7. The 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose shall be installed in 2" PVC conduit between pullbox and entry to pavement slab. Loop shall be attached to top of reinforcing bars when used in the pavement slab.

title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop
summary: Shows a preformed detector loop for new embedded light rail track, with 4 turns of wire installed in a 2" Schedule 80 PVC conduit 30" deep to a termination pullbox. No rebar or metal other than the track rails may be placed within 3 feet horizontally or vertically of the loop. The preformed loop uses 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, #16 TFFN wire, a 5" expansion joint, and rubberized asphalt fill.

sheets.notes:
LRT detector for new track (embedded)
4 turns of wire. 30". Embedded track. Termination pullbox. P.C.C. or asphalt concrete. Detector handhole type A. Subbase. Termination pull box. Preformed loop. Subballast bed. 2" PVC Sched. 80 conduit 30" deep. Section: embedded track.

Notes:
1. Preformed loop to be used for new installations in embedded track.
2. No rebar or metal of any kind other than the track rails shall be placed within three feet (3') horizontally or vertically from LRT loop.
3. See page 2 and 3 for preformed LRT loop details.

LRT preformed loop details
Notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, with an O.D. of 3/4 inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wire in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose, seamless, with fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.

Plan: Cover and frame. 2-3/4" brass lift plug (2). SIGNAL, 1" stamped letters. Dimensions A (cover outside), B (frame inside), C (frame inside dim.), D.
Section: 1/8" (typ.). 3/16" plate. Cover. 1/2" x 1/2" continuous steel bar. End and mid-point (typ.). 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical all sides. 8 degree slope. Frame. Typical all four (4) sides of frame and cover. Height 1-13/16".
Steel sleeve internal thread 3/4"-10 UNC full length to match brass lift plug. Slot 3/8" square and 3/8" deep. 3/16" steel plate.
Installed: sidewalk grade, frame inside C and G, pull box, 4" x 3/16" steel plate typical all sides.

Dimensions
For Type 2 pullbox: A 18-3/4", B 19", C 29", D 9-1/2", E 28-3/4", F 28-1/4", G 27-7/8".
For Type 3 pullbox: A 25-3/4", B 26", C 38", D 13", E 37-3/4", F 37-1/4", G 36-7/8".

Notes:
1. All metal surfaces for special frame and cover shall have a galvanized finish.
2. All welding, machining and drilling shall be done before galvanizing.
3. Plug threads must be greased thoroughly prior to installation.
